define.question: What should I build first?
define.answer: One operator, one ticket inbox and one read-only investigation. You do not need a database or cloud account to explore the product sketch.
define.try: Try asking: “Which information would let an operator decide their next safe check?” Write that down before choosing a model.
define.remember: The coding assistant creates the source; the runtime agent is the program the finished app calls.

build.question: My preview looks good. Am I done?
build.answer: Create a new synthetic ticket, search for its title, filter it out, clear the filter and select it again. A screenshot alone cannot prove these controls work.
build.try: If a control is decorative, ask the builder to implement only that interaction and retest it. Keep the AI panel disconnected until the controls work.
build.remember: A hosted builder preview cannot reach a server bound to your laptop’s 127.0.0.1 address.

agent.question: Why does Analyze safely fail?
agent.answer: Check whether the request reaches your own server, then inspect its sanitized error. Confirm the exact configured model alias, authentication binding and native tool support.
agent.try: Start with one ordinary greeting, then one health question. Change one setting at a time; never substitute a canned answer for a failed model call.
agent.remember: The server chooses the model and looks up the session-owned ticket. Never accept an endpoint or a key from the browser.

trace.question: How do I know the answer belongs to this ticket?
trace.answer: Create a fresh synthetic ticket, select it and run analysis. Inspect the submitted ticket ID, actual server lookup and tool evidence. Clear stale results when selecting a different ticket.
trace.try: Repeat the journey once in the actual app. An answer shown only in a terminal or a static preview does not pass the app check.
trace.remember: The app must work by the end of Part 1. Full export/readback is added in Part 4.

secure.question: The app stays busy after an error. What should I check?
secure.answer: Inspect the request lifecycle and cleanup path. Both successful and failed responses must clear the busy state and display the actual outcome.
secure.try: Use an isolated model double or controlled failed request, not a service shutdown. Ensure a later permitted request can run.
secure.remember: A canned answer is not recovery. Keep real failures visible; add broader security regression tests in Part 5.

host.question: Do I need OCI to complete the first hour?
host.answer: No. You can finish the local app and explain its target architecture. A live hosted invocation needs your own scoped tenancy, identity, image and network path.
host.try: Save the source baseline, exact start/stop command and private config requirements. Restart the app locally before proceeding to Part 2. OCI hosting is added in Part 6.
host.remember: The local Studio and hosted coordinator have different request protocols. An adapter and authentication are required; replacing a URL is not a migration.
